# The invoice again, re-posted with a `from_credit:` block naming the split its
# own unpost left loose.
#
# This is what a reader is led to write. Unposting leaves the money in a lot of
# the customer's, so `find-prepayments` lists it and the export writes an
# `open_prepayment:` block for it — both saying, correctly, that the money is
# the customer's and unattached. Spending an owner's credit is what a
# `from_credit:` block is for.
#
# But a bank paid this one, and the split says so by not saying otherwise: a
# settlement that really came out of credit carries `applied_from_credit`, and
# this one does not. Believed, the block would write `from_credit: true` onto a
# bank payment and take the account and date it arrived by out of the export.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.

invoice "INV-USD-RETARGET"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-01-05
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-05
		description: "Consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-05
		due: 2026-02-05
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-RETARGET"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		amount: 100
		from_credit: true
		credit_dated: 2026-02-25
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		txn_split_guid: "SPLIT_GUID"
		memo: "Payment for INV-USD-RETARGET"
